segments.text: Welcome to your daily Robotics news digest for September 11, 2026.
Today we cover AI teaching robots, robotaxi tech, and the future of robotics with ChatGPT.
Tune in for the highlights.
From NVIDIA Blog, "Skild AI Taps NVIDIA Physical AI to Teach Robots New Tasks From a Single Video".
This report details how the Skild AI foundation model learns new, long-horizon tasks from a single video demonstration through in-context learning.
The system demonstrated the ability to interpret demonstrated intent and sequences to execute unfamiliar tasks such as plant potting and assembly without explicit programming.
This approach yielded a significant advantage over other AI systems in learning complex, multi-step manipulations, reducing the need for extensive manual training.
The process leverages NVIDIA's AI infrastructure, simulation, and robotics frameworks to advance adaptable robot intelligence.
This development suggests a pathway toward more adaptable robot intelligence by utilizing real-world experience for future model development.
From NVIDIA Blog, "Physical AI Takes the Wheel: How the World’s Robotaxi Leaders Are Building With NVIDIA Technologies".
This report details how the world's robotaxi leaders are utilizing NVIDIA technologies to develop autonomous driving systems for the projected $400 billion robotaxi market by 2035.
The development necessitates a comprehensive computing solution incorporating AI training, simulation, and in-vehicle computing.

Robotaxi leaders are integrating NVIDIA technologies such as the DGX platform, Omniverse for simulation, and DRIVE Hyperion for in-vehicle systems across major automotive partners to create intelligent autonomous fleets.
This multi-faceted approach facilitates the necessary development of safe and scalable driverless technology.
The integration of these tools establishes a foundational architecture for autonomous deployment in the automotive sector.
This trend signifies a substantial industry shift toward hardware-accelerated, comprehensive AI solutions in transportation.
From TheSequence, "The Sequence Opinion - Issue 931: Robotics Is Waiting for Its ChatGPT Moment"
reports on the potential for robots to achieve a "ChatGPT moment" by learning through conversation and examples to perform complex tasks.
Generalist robot models are increasing the credibility of this prospect by demonstrating versatility in their capabilities.
The report details that the primary challenge remaining involves developing the necessary learning, control, and economic frameworks for robots to operate effectively in novel environments.
The analysis suggests that similar to large language models, robotics requires a persuasive encounter with versatility extending beyond mere language to achieve this capability.
The focus is directed toward enabling machines to translate linguistic input into effective physical action.
This shift indicates that future development in the AI and technology sector will concentrate on robust methods for physical execution based on advanced language understanding.
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: ROSCon Global 2026 Sponsors and Exhibitors"
reports on the confirmed sponsors and exhibitors for ROSCon Global 2026, detailing the organizational structure supporting the event.
Platinum sponsors include major entities such as AMD, NVIDIA, and Intel, while Gold sponsors encompass Canonical, Clearpath, and Intel, alongside several other organizations.
Silver and Bronze sponsors include companies like AgileX, Autodesk, and Autoware, with Startup Alley featuring sponsors like 10Things and Botbot.
This structure confirms the involvement of key industry players across various tiers for the upcoming global conference.
The sponsorship levels facilitate attendee engagement through on-site presence, presentations, and demonstrations.
This demonstrates the significant industry backing for the future development and dissemination of robotics software.
From IEEE Spectrum - Robotics, "Robots Are Learning to Feel".
This report details the challenges in robot manipulation due to a lack of tactile feedback and the progress being made to incorporate this sensory information into robot learning.

Researchers are addressing the limitation that robots experience in handling deformable objects and small items because current vision-language-action models struggle with fine-grained control due to the omission of tactile data.
To address this, efforts are focused on creating specialized tactile datasets and models to integrate this sensory information into robot learning.
The utilization of expert submodels for rapid tactile control has yielded advancements in complex manipulation tasks, demonstrating higher success rates.
Future progress in this area depends on expanding the diversity of tactile data and developing effective methods for fusing visual and tactile information.
This development signals a shift towards more physically realistic and capable robotic interaction.
And that's all the circuits for today!
Hope your algorithms are running smoothly.
Go forth and code with curiosity.
See you tomorrow for the next byte!
